candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — elopement/security precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Respond to identified elopement risk with risk-based preventive precautions, including appropriate observation and environmental/access controls, rather than waiting for an actual exit attempt.

options.A: Continue routine observation until the client makes an actual exit attempt because questions about doors alone do not justify activating precautions.
options.B: Use the unit's elopement-risk process to implement preventive precautions appropriate to the assessed risk, such as enhanced observation and environmental or access controls.
options.C: Move the client closer to the nurses' station but leave the usual observation level unchanged because location alone is sufficient to manage the risk.
options.D: Document the concern and ask family to reinforce staying on the unit, but defer environmental precautions unless the client reaches an exit.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ PSNet describes elopement prevention as a combination of risk assessment and preventive precautions. For at-risk patients, precautions may include observation protocols and, in mental-health settings, environmental or access controls such as alarms or automatic door locks. B applies that principle without prescribing a single universal intervention. A and D wait for an actual attempt, while C relies on location alone rather than an appropriate risk-based precaution plan.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Patients should be assessed for elopement risk and at-risk patients placed on special preventive precautions; preventive measures may include enhanced observation and environmental/access controls appropriate to the setting.
candidate.source_locator: Elopement commentary — sections on assessing elopement risk, preventive precautions, observation protocols, and environmental/access controls; Take-Home Points.
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) PSNet

candidate.stem: An inpatient psychiatric client repeatedly asks about exit locations and how visitor badges open doors. Which nursing action best addresses the identified elopement risk?
